checks.evidence: The new template equals the previous template after exactly its four declared reader-role substitutions. Both stored template hashes verify. The controlling same-entry policy and atom grading rules are unchanged; the new gate explicitly allows only the completed frozen assigned reader and withholds feedback from still-live blind readers.

checks.area: Complete disjoint role blocks and all atoms
checks.evidence: Synthetic 113-entry and 53-entry banks produced complete disjoint blocks of15–20 entries. Assigned IDs and all four requested atoms per synthetic entry were validated. Missing/duplicate/wrong requirements and malformed/missing/duplicate/reordered grade IDs were rejected.

checks.area: All same-entry substantive fields and quotations
checks.evidence: Quotes from answer, ledger fact, plain case conclusion and operative evidence were all accepted. Empty, metadata-only, other-role and cross-question quotations were rejected. A Correct label with an omitted atom and invalid statuses were rejected. This verifies artifact consistency, not semantic correctness of synthetic or real grading decisions.

Raw/question/key/scope/packet tampering was rejected. Full entry equality still rejected a changed packet when its packet hash was updated. Report-role/block mismatches, altered frozen collections and reports changed after collection were rejected. Exclusive creation prevented overwrite of role collections/proofs/results; originals stayed intact.

A could be prepared/validated/collected with B absent, while combine required B. After both synthetic roles were collected, the adapter’s final result exactly equaled direct invocation of the original paired prepare/merge machinery on the same frozen inputs and reports. All original independent reports and complete raw entries were preserved.

Full expected summary/metadata/original role entries passed. Partial raw entries, missing/wrong metadata, other-role-only replacements, missing summary lines, recognized early writes and recognized status calls failed as expected. The four counterexamples show that the stronger timing/isolation/original-source claims are not yet fully established.

concrete_findings.problem: The first-write boundary is inferred from a short substring list rather than actual artifact-write events. A valid file-write spelling not on that list permits later inputs to be counted as pre-write delivery; a stdout-only serialization spelling on the list stops evidence collection even though it does not write an artifact.
synthetic_observations: A first call containing open(..., "x").write(...) followed by all inputs was certified complete; the early write was not detected.
A call containing json.dump(entry, sys.stdout, ...) was treated as a first output write, causing a false incomplete proof.
concrete_findings.impact: The proof cannot reliably certify that complete original inputs preceded the first artifact write. This is a proof-boundary problem, not a reader content-grade finding.
concrete_findings.recommendation: Use an explicitly auditable artifact-write event/helper or a tightly specified write interface, and distinguish stdout transport from file writes. Unrecognized possible mutation paths must not silently yield a complete proof. Preserve existing logs/artifacts and issue a separate verification attempt.

concrete_findings.problem: The proof verifies the presence of expected role inputs but does not reject additional other-role packet entries. An extra foreign-role entry is ignored while completeness remains true.
synthetic_observations: Other-role-only input correctly failed to replace the expected entry.
When full assigned-role inputs were present, an additional separate packet-shaped entry containing the opposite reader role still yielded complete_input_delivery_confirmed=true.
concrete_findings.impact: Completeness alone is being reported without detecting this concrete violation of the role-isolation input boundary. The single-reader packet producer itself correctly supplies only the assigned reader.
concrete_findings.recommendation: Account for visible packet-shaped inputs and source-read calls, rejecting other-role/foreign packet material outside the approved complete entry. Avoid flagging metadata-like text that is legitimately inside an already approved original entry. Keep completeness and forbidden-extra-input checks explicit.

concrete_findings.problem: The proof compares visible objects to the current packet but does not verify that packet against its frozen manifest hash, original role-entry hashes or input hashes. Its returned packet_sha256 is informational, not compared with the manifest.
synthetic_observations: Removing a custom nested field from a packet’s role entry, then delivering that altered packet exactly, was certified complete despite the frozen manifest still binding the original packet.
The per-reader grading validator separately rejected that same tampered packet.
concrete_findings.impact: The proof can incorrectly claim complete ORIGINAL role input delivery when it has only proved delivery of a cropped or altered current packet. Existing validate_role guards prevent this particular packet tampering from silently reaching a valid final aggregation when those guards are run.
concrete_findings.recommendation: Before certifying delivery, verify frozen input/packet hashes and full role-entry canonical hashes, and bind role/block identity to the role manifest. Compare with the frozen original assigned-role entry as needed, without reading the still-blind other reader.

concrete_findings.component: prove-bounded-delivery.py: text_present(), inherited summary delivery check
concrete_findings.problem: Summary lines are accepted as arbitrary substrings of all visible output. A changed line with the original as a proper prefix is falsely counted as complete original summary delivery.
synthetic_observations: With a synthetic summary frozen and prepared as Value 1, a visible line Value 10 satisfied the original Value 1 line check. All metadata and original entries were otherwise delivered, and the proof certified complete. This test used a matching frozen summary manifest, independently of SRG-03.
concrete_findings.impact: The proof can certify an altered quantity or condition as an exact original summary line.
concrete_findings.recommendation: Validate a defined full-line/chunk delivery representation with exact boundaries, decoded content and source line ranges/hashes. Support intentional line-number prefixes/JSON transport explicitly rather than relying on unconstrained substring containment.

review_limits: Only the six permitted static helper/template files and this reviewer’s own newly created synthetic harness/results were read.

No actual summary, bank, questions, key, scope, reader, grade, result, provenance, history, runtime session or status inputs were read. All such file names inside tests referred exclusively to an in-memory filesystem.

Both adapter and imported paired-module ROOT/Path globals, plus delivery adapter and imported bounded-proof globals, pointed at the same /synthetic virtual root before helper operations. Import-loading top-level code was not executed; allowed function definitions were compiled directly.
The tests establish code paths and integrity checks, not actual reader factual correctness, model attention, terminal lifecycle or live-run isolation. No actual score was requested or inferred.
Immutable dispatch/terminal/model and final canonical gates remain coordinator responsibilities; this review introduces no gameplay facts, key changes, per-question hints or grading-policy changes.
Source files/templates were not edited. All real writes were confined to the authorized new review subfolder and the two requested root review outputs.
required_change_scope: Strengthen the delivery proof’s event boundary, foreign-input detection, frozen source binding and exact summary-content checks. Keep structural/proof failures separate from content grades and do not alter original reports, entries, asked atoms or grading semantics.
